second_order: co-ordinating where and how to make the Saltire
theme_note: These codes make a shared job practical by choosing locations, coordinates, proportions, work divisions and who is still working; what varies is whether the proposal starts a flag, redirects an existing effort or checks participation.
regrouped_from: Grouping reviewed across all slices: kept apart from venue consolidation because deciding the design and moving the discussion are different practices.

second_order: arguing over turning the Union Jack into a Saltire
theme_note: These codes contest the same proposed practice—recolouring or attacking the Union Jack—with calls, attempted changes, reports of resistance and direct refusals to help; disagreement is part of the practice rather than evidence of a settled position.
regrouped_from: Grouping reviewed across all slices: calls and refusals remain together because they contest the same proposed conversion; kept apart from ordinary repair.

second_order: making politics out of the picture
theme_note: These passages attach Scottish, British, independence and EU meanings or jokes to the canvas; they vary from labels and taunts to explicit rejection of using the art for a political agenda.
regrouped_from: Grouping reviewed across all slices: kept apart from the Union-Jack dispute because political joking and interpretation also occur without a proposed attack.

second_order: posting and policing April Fools patter
theme_note: These codes perform fake local headlines and then test, dismiss or redirect the patter; the shared practice is making and policing the room's own April Fools conduct, not acting on the canvas.
regrouped_from: Grouping reviewed across all slices: kept separate because these are the subreddit's own April Fools performances, explicitly not canvas conduct.

second_order: getting the Saltire sorted, fixed and defended
theme_note: These passages treat the Saltire as work needing proportion, repair, watching or defence; some raise alarms, others diagnose friendly damage or correct an alarm, so the threat is not assumed to be external.
regrouped_from: Grouping reviewed across all slices: alarms, corrections, repairs and watching remain together as maintaining the shared work; additions were separated.

second_order: celebrating and taking stock of what they made
theme_note: These codes publicly mark progress, completion, loss and shared effort; they range from 'coming along nicely' to thanks, final images, mourning and awkward retrospective jokes.
regrouped_from: Grouping reviewed across all slices: progress reports, thanks, mourning and final accounting remain together as publicly marking what the work became.

second_order: putting the weird pixel shit in one sticky and Discord
theme_note: These passages gather scattered pixel talk into a pinned or sticky thread and Discord, redirect duplicate posts, and carry reports back; what varies is whether the move is invited, enforced by moderators or acknowledged by posters.
regrouped_from: Grouping reviewed across all slices: sticky, pin and Discord codes remain together as concentrating discussion; design decisions reported from those venues stay with this practice only when the move itself is foregrounded.

second_order: making room and deals with neighbours
theme_note: These codes ask for room, settle borders, offer reciprocal help or refuse when another design threatens theirs; the practice holds accommodation and conflict together without treating every claimed ally as independently verified.
regrouped_from: Grouping reviewed across all slices: border requests, restraint, reciprocal help and disputes remain together as working out room with named neighbours.

second_order: explaining the canvas and its patter
theme_note: These exchanges answer newcomers' questions about the one-pixel canvas, timing and visible patter; they vary between full explanations, thanks and requests to identify a pictured detail.
regrouped_from: Grouping reviewed across all slices: retained as a distinct exchange practice because it brings newcomers into the room's canvas talk.

second_order: adding Scottish things around the Saltire
theme_note: These codes extend the Saltire with thistles, Nessie, captions, hearts, borders, cans, tartan and other Scottish marks; the shared practice is proposing and revising additions, not the surface similarity of the objects.
regrouped_from: Grouping reviewed across all slices: grouped by the practice of extending the Scottish scene, while repair and defence remain separate.

second_order: using scripts, spare placements and timer workarounds
theme_note: These passages describe gaining extra placements or bypassing the timer; they form a small distinct practice because they change how pixels can be placed rather than what should be drawn.
regrouped_from: Grouping reviewed across all slices: retained as a single-code theme at founding and extended only by another explicit timer bypass.

second_order: carrying place cooperation into what came next
theme_note: These late passages turn the finished event into withdrawal-driven continuation and a proposed cultural exchange credited to r/place cooperation; the outcomes of both moves remain beyond the in-window record.
regrouped_from: Grouping reviewed across all slices: retained as a late distinct practice because it carries the event into a successor activity and inter-community exchange rather than accounting for the finished canvas.
